items.prompt: Following the order of operations, find the value of −6 + 24 ÷ (−3) × 2 − (−5).
items.explain:
Do multiplication and division from left to right first, then addition and subtraction.

24 ÷ (−3) = −8

−8 × 2 = −16

−6 + (−16) − (−5) = −6 − 16 + 5 = −17

−5 comes from multiplying (−3) × 2 before dividing, which breaks the left-to-right rule: 24 ÷ (−6) = −4, then −6 − 4 + 5 = −5. −27 comes from treating −(−5) as −5 instead of +5.
why: You multiplied (−3) × 2 before dividing: 24 ÷ (−6) = −4. Multiplication and division go left to right, so 24 ÷ (−3) = −8 comes first.
You treated −(−5) as −5. Subtracting a negative adds: −6 − 16 + 5 = −17.
You treated 24 ÷ (−3) as +8. A positive divided by a negative is negative: −8 × 2 = −16.

items.prompt: A carpenter cuts blocking pieces that are each 1¼ feet long from a board that is 8¾ feet long. If there is no waste, how many pieces can she cut from the board?
items.explain:
Divide the board length by the piece length.

8¾ = 35/4 and 1¼ = 5/4

35/4 ÷ 5/4 = 35/4 × 4/5 = 140/20 = 7

Check: 7 × 1¼ = 7 + 7/4 = 7 + 1¾ = 8¾ feet.

A common error is to divide only the whole numbers, 8 ÷ 1 = 8. The fractional parts must be included.

mistakes.why: You divided only the whole numbers (8 ÷ 1). Include the fractions: 35/4 ÷ 5/4 = 7.
You multiplied the lengths. To find how many pieces fit, divide the board length by the piece length: 8.75 ÷ 1.25 = 7.

items.prompt:
Which expression is equivalent to the expression below for all x ≠ 0?

(2x3)2 · x4 ÷ (4x5)
items.explain:
Power of a product: (2x3)2 = 22 · x3×2 = 4x6

Multiply by x4 (add exponents): 4x6 · x4 = 4x10

Divide by 4x5 (divide coefficients, subtract exponents): 4x10 ÷ 4x5 = x5

(1/2)x5 comes from forgetting to square the 2, so the numerator becomes 2x10. x4 comes from adding the exponents 3 + 2 instead of multiplying them.
why: You added the exponents 3 + 2 instead of multiplying them. (x<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>6</sup>, so the result is x<sup>6 + 4 − 5</sup> = x<sup>5</sup>.
You forgot to square the 2, so the numerator became 2x<sup>10</sup>. (2x<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 4x<sup>6</sup>, and 4 ÷ 4 = 1.
You multiplied the exponents when multiplying x<sup>6</sup> · x<sup>4</sup> (6 × 4 = 24). When multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents: x<sup>10</sup>.

items.prompt: Solve for x: (2x + 1)/5 = (x − 4)/2
items.explain:
Multiply both sides by 10, the least common denominator:

10 × (2x + 1)/5 = 10 × (x − 4)/2

2(2x + 1) = 5(x − 4)

4x + 2 = 5x − 20

Subtract 4x from both sides: 2 = x − 20

Add 20: x = 22

Check: (2(22) + 1)/5 = 45/5 = 9 and (22 − 4)/2 = 18/2 = 9.

21 comes from multiplying only the 2x by 2 on the left (4x + 1). 6 comes from multiplying only the x by 5 on the right (5x − 4).
why: You multiplied only the 2x by 2 on the left, getting 4x + 1. Distribute to every term: 2(2x + 1) = 4x + 2.
You multiplied only the x by 5 on the right, getting 5x − 4. Distribute: 5(x − 4) = 5x − 20.
You reached −x = −22 and stopped. Divide both sides by −1 to get x = 22.

items.prompt: Which number is between 7 and 8 on the number line?
items.explain:
Square the endpoints: 72 = 49 and 82 = 64. A square root lies between 7 and 8 only if the number under the root is between 49 and 64.

50 is between 49 and 64, so √50 is between 7 and 8 (about 7.07).

√48 is just under 7 because 48 < 49. √65 and √70 are greater than 8 because 65 and 70 are greater than 64.
why: 48 is less than 49 = 7<sup>2</sup>, so √48 is just under 7, not between 7 and 8.
65 is greater than 64 = 8<sup>2</sup>, so √65 is a little more than 8.
70 is greater than 64 = 8<sup>2</sup>, so √70 is about 8.4, more than 8.

items.prompt: A contractor bid $8,600 to build a backyard patio. Because material prices rose, the final bill was $9,890. By what percent did the final bill exceed the bid?
items.explain:
Amount over the bid: 9,890 − 8,600 = $1,290.

Percent change = change ÷ original = 1,290 ÷ 8,600 = 0.15 = 15%.

13% comes from dividing by the final bill (1,290 ÷ 9,890 ≈ 0.13). Percent change always divides by the original amount, which here is the bid. 115% compares the whole final bill to the bid instead of only the increase.
why: You divided the increase by the final bill (1,290 ÷ 9,890). Percent change divides by the original amount, the bid: 1,290 ÷ 8,600.
115% compares the whole final bill to the bid. The increase is 115% − 100% = 15%.
You wrote the $1,290 increase as 1.29% without dividing by the bid. Percent change = 1,290 ÷ 8,600 = 0.15.

items.prompt: A landscaping supplier sells sod at a price of $147 for 350 square feet. At this rate, how much will 1,250 square feet of sod cost, in dollars?
items.explain:
Find the unit price: 147 ÷ 350 = $0.42 per square foot.

Multiply by the area needed: 0.42 × 1,250 = $525.

You can also use a proportion: 147/350 = c/1,250, so 350c = 147 × 1,250 = 183,750 and c = 525.

mistakes.why: $0.42 is the price for one square foot. Multiply by the 1,250 square feet needed: 0.42 × 1,250 = $525.
You set up the proportion upside down (350/147 = c/1,250). Keep dollars over square feet on both sides: 147/350 = c/1,250.

items.prompt: A crew is laying pavers for the L-shaped patio shown below. All corners are right angles. What is the area of the patio?

figure.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 300 210' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><polygon points='40,30 160,30 160,90 240,90 240,170 40,170' fill='#F3E9C9' stroke='#0A1F3D' stroke-width='2'/><text x='85' y='22' font-size='14' fill='#0A1F3D'>12 ft</text><text x='166' y='65' font-size='14' fill='#0A1F3D'>6 ft</text><text x='186' y='84' font-size='14' fill='#0A1F3D'>8 ft</text><text x='246' y='135' font-size='14' fill='#0A1F3D'>8 ft</text><text x='122' y='190' font-size='14' fill='#0A1F3D'>20 ft</text><text x='2' y='105' font-size='14' fill='#0A1F3D'>14 ft</text></svg>
figure.alt: An L-shaped patio. The bottom side is 20 ft and the left side is 14 ft. The top side is 12 ft. A notch is cut from the top right corner: it goes down 6 ft and then across 8 ft. The remaining right side is 8 ft.

items.explain:
Think of the patio as a 20 ft by 14 ft rectangle with an 8 ft by 6 ft corner removed.

Large rectangle: 20 × 14 = 280 square feet

Missing corner: 8 × 6 = 48 square feet

Patio: 280 − 48 = 232 square feet

Check another way: split into a 12 ft by 14 ft piece (168) and an 8 ft by 8 ft piece (64): 168 + 64 = 232.

280 ignores the missing corner, 328 adds the corner instead of subtracting it, and 68 feet is the perimeter, not the area.
why: 280 is the full 20 ft by 14 ft rectangle. Subtract the missing 8 ft by 6 ft corner: 280 − 48 = 232.
You added the 48-square-foot corner instead of subtracting it. The corner is cut out of the rectangle.
68 feet is the perimeter, the distance around. Area counts square feet inside.

items.prompt: A concrete slab for a shed will be 24 feet long, 18 feet wide, and 4 inches thick. Concrete is ordered in cubic yards (1 cubic yard = 27 cubic feet). About how many cubic yards of concrete are needed for the slab?
items.explain:
Change the thickness to feet: 4 inches = 4/12 = 1/3 foot.

Volume in cubic feet: 24 × 18 × 1/3 = 432 × 1/3 = 144 cubic feet.

Change to cubic yards: 144 ÷ 27 ≈ 5.3 cubic yards.

64 comes from leaving the thickness as 4 (inches) with the other sides in feet: 24 × 18 × 4 = 1,728, and 1,728 ÷ 27 = 64. 16 comes from dividing by 9, which converts square feet, not cubic feet. 144 is the volume in cubic feet.
why: You divided 144 cubic feet by 9. Nine converts square feet to square yards; for cubic feet to cubic yards, divide by 27.
You left the thickness as 4 (inches) while the other sides were in feet. Change 4 inches to 1/3 foot first.
144 is the volume in cubic feet. Divide by 27 to get cubic yards: 144 ÷ 27 ≈ 5.3.

items.prompt: A fence post will be set in a hole shaped like a cylinder. The hole has a diameter of 12 inches and a depth of 4 feet. What is the volume of the hole, to the nearest hundredth of a cubic foot?
items.explain:
Use the formula sheet: V = πr2h.

Use feet for every measure. Diameter = 12 inches = 1 foot, so the radius r = 0.5 foot. Depth h = 4 feet.

V = π(0.5)2(4) = π(0.25)(4) = π ≈ 3.14 cubic feet

12.57 comes from using the 1-foot diameter as the radius: π(1)2(4) = 4π. 452.39 comes from mixing units, using r = 6 inches with h = 4 feet: π(36)(4).
why: You used the 1-foot diameter as the radius: π(1)<sup>2</sup>(4) = 4π. The radius is half the diameter, 0.5 foot.
You forgot to square the radius: π(0.5)(4) = 2π. Use r<sup>2</sup> = 0.25.
You mixed units, using r = 6 inches with h = 4 feet. Change all measures to feet first: r = 0.5 foot.

items.prompt: A delivered pile of mulch is shaped like a cone. The base of the pile has a diameter of 10 feet, and the pile is 6 feet tall. What is the volume of the pile, to the nearest cubic foot?
items.explain:
Use the formula sheet: V = (1/3)πr2h.

The radius is half the diameter: r = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 feet.

V = (1/3)π(5)2(6) = (1/3)π(25)(6) = 50π ≈ 157.08

To the nearest cubic foot: 157 cubic feet.

Leaving out the 1/3 gives 150π ≈ 471, which is the volume of a cylinder, not a cone. Using 10 as the radius gives 200π ≈ 628.

mistakes.why: You left out the 1/3, which gives the volume of a cylinder. A cone is (1/3)πr<sup>2</sup>h = 50π ≈ 157.
You used the 10-foot diameter as the radius. The radius is 5 feet: (1/3)π(25)(6) = 50π.
50 is the coefficient of π (50π). Multiply by π to get the volume: 50π ≈ 157 cubic feet.

items.prompt: A closed cylindrical water tank has a radius of 2 feet and a height of 5 feet. The entire outside of the tank, including the top and bottom, will be painted. What is the surface area to be painted, to the nearest tenth of a square foot?
items.explain:
Use the formula sheet: SA = 2πrh + 2πr2.

Side (lateral area): 2π(2)(5) = 20π

Top and bottom: 2π(2)2 = 8π

Total: 20π + 8π = 28π ≈ 88.0 square feet

62.8 is only the side (20π). 75.4 includes only one circular end (20π + 4π = 24π). 226.2 comes from using the diameter, 4, as the radius.
why: 62.8 is only the side (2πrh = 20π). A closed tank also has a top and a bottom: add 2πr<sup>2</sup> = 8π.
75.4 includes only one circular end (20π + 4π). The tank has both a top and a bottom.
You used the diameter, 4, as the radius. With r = 2, SA = 20π + 8π = 28π.

items.prompt: A roof rafter forms the slanted side of a right triangle. The rise of the roof is 6 feet and the horizontal run is 14 feet. To the nearest tenth of a foot, how long is the rafter?
items.explain:
The rafter is the hypotenuse c, and the rise and run are the legs.

c2 = 62 + 142 = 36 + 196 = 232

c = √232 ≈ 15.2 feet

20.0 adds the legs (6 + 14) without squaring. 12.6 subtracts the squares (√160), which finds a leg, not the hypotenuse. 232 is c2; the square root was not taken.
why: You added the legs (6 + 14) without squaring. Use c<sup>2</sup> = 6<sup>2</sup> + 14<sup>2</sup>.
You subtracted the squares (√160), which finds a leg. The rafter is the hypotenuse, so add the squares.
232 is c<sup>2</sup>. Take the square root: √232 ≈ 15.2 feet.

items.prompt: A circular stone patio has a circumference of 47.1 feet. Using 3.14 for π, what is the area of the patio, to the nearest tenth of a square foot?
items.explain:
Find the radius from the circumference: C = 2πr, so 47.1 = 2(3.14)r = 6.28r and r = 47.1 ÷ 6.28 = 7.5 feet.

Area: A = πr2 = 3.14 × 7.52 = 3.14 × 56.25 = 176.625 ≈ 176.6 square feet.

706.5 uses the diameter, 15, as the radius (3.14 × 225). 353.3 multiplies the circumference by the radius (47.1 × 7.5) instead of taking half of that product. 23.6 is πr, which is not squared.
why: You used the diameter, 15, as the radius (3.14 × 225). The radius is 47.1 ÷ 6.28 = 7.5.
You multiplied the circumference by the radius (47.1 × 7.5). Area is πr<sup>2</sup> = 3.14 × 56.25.
23.6 is πr (3.14 × 7.5). The radius must be squared: 3.14 × 7.5<sup>2</sup>.

items.prompt: On a landscape plan, the scale is ¼ inch = 2 feet. A garden bed is 3¾ inches long on the plan. What is the actual length of the garden bed?
items.explain:
Find how many ¼-inch units are in 3¾ inches: 3.75 ÷ 0.25 = 15.

Each ¼ inch stands for 2 feet: 15 × 2 = 30 feet.

Another way: ¼ inch = 2 feet means 1 inch = 8 feet, and 3.75 × 8 = 30.

7.5 feet comes from multiplying 3.75 by 2 as if 1 inch = 2 feet. 15 is the number of quarter inches, not feet.
why: You multiplied 3.75 by 2, as if 1 inch = 2 feet. The scale is 1/4 inch = 2 feet, so 1 inch = 8 feet.
15 is the number of quarter inches, not feet. Each quarter inch stands for 2 feet: 15 × 2 = 30.
You multiplied the 15 quarter inches by 4 instead of by 2. Each quarter inch stands for 2 feet.

items.prompt:
A concrete crew recorded the amount of concrete it poured each day for five days, in cubic yards:

6.5, 8, 7.25, 9, 8.25

What is the mean amount poured per day, in cubic yards?
items.explain:
Add the values: 6.5 + 8 + 7.25 + 9 + 8.25 = 39.

Divide by the number of days: 39 ÷ 5 = 7.8 cubic yards.

The median of these values is 8, so be careful not to confuse the two measures.

mistakes.why: 8 is the median (middle value). The mean is the sum divided by the count: 39 ÷ 5 = 7.8.
39 is the total for all five days. Divide by 5 days to get the mean: 7.8.
You divided by 4 instead of 5. There are five days of data: 39 ÷ 5 = 7.8.

items.prompt:
A carpenter has seven boards with these lengths, in feet:

12, 8, 16, 10, 14, 8, 20

Which statement about the board lengths is true?
options: The median is 12 feet and the range is 12 feet.
The median is 10 feet and the range is 12 feet.
The median is 12 feet and the range is 20 feet.
The median is 12.6 feet and the range is 12 feet.
items.explain:
Put the lengths in order: 8, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20.

Median: with 7 values, the middle (4th) value is 12 feet.

Range: greatest − least = 20 − 8 = 12 feet.

10 feet is the middle of the list before it is put in order. A range of 20 uses only the greatest value. 12.6 is about the mean (88 ÷ 7 ≈ 12.57), not the median.
why: 10 is the middle of the list before it is sorted. Order the values first: 8, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, so the median is 12.
20 is the greatest value, not the range. Range = 20 − 8 = 12.
12.6 is about the mean (88 ÷ 7), not the median. The median is the middle value, 12.

items.prompt: A bin holds 40 bolts: 25 are zinc, 10 are stainless steel, and 5 are brass. A worker takes one bolt at random, keeps it, and then takes a second bolt at random. What is the probability that both bolts are stainless steel?
items.explain:
First bolt: P(stainless) = 10/40.

The first bolt is not replaced, so 9 stainless bolts remain among 39. Second bolt: P(stainless) = 9/39.

P(both) = 10/40 × 9/39 = 90/1,560 = 3/52 (about 0.058).

1/16 is (10/40)2, the answer if the first bolt were put back. 1/4 is the probability for only one bolt. 1/2 adds the two probabilities 1/4 + 1/4 instead of multiplying.
why: 1/16 = (10/40)<sup>2</sup> assumes the first bolt is put back. It is kept, so the second draw is 9/39.
1/4 is the chance for one bolt only. Both bolts must be stainless: 10/40 × 9/39.
You added the probabilities. For two events that both must happen, multiply them.

items.prompt: For each front yard in a new development, the builder lets buyers choose 1 of 4 kinds of trees, 1 of 3 kinds of shrubs, and 1 of 5 kinds of ground cover. How many different yard designs are possible?
items.explain:
Use the counting principle: multiply the number of choices at each step.

4 × 3 × 5 = 60 designs.

12 adds the choices (4 + 3 + 5) instead of multiplying. 20 and 15 multiply only two of the three choices.
why: You added the choices (4 + 3 + 5). For a choice at each step, multiply: 4 × 3 × 5.
20 = 4 × 5 leaves out the 3 shrub choices.
15 = 3 × 5 leaves out the 4 tree choices.

items.prompt: A grain of sand has a mass of about 6.7 × 10−4 gram. A truckload of sand has a mass of about 2.2 × 107 grams. About how many grains of sand are in the truckload?
items.explain:
Divide the total mass by the mass of one grain:

(2.2 × 107) ÷ (6.7 × 10−4) = (2.2 ÷ 6.7) × 107 − (−4) ≈ 0.328 × 1011

Rewrite in scientific notation: 0.328 × 1011 = 3.3 × 1010 (about 33 billion grains).

3.3 × 103 subtracts the exponents as 7 − 4 instead of 7 − (−4). 1.5 × 104 multiplies the two numbers instead of dividing. 3.3 × 1011 forgets to lower the exponent when 0.328 is changed to 3.28.
why: You subtracted the exponents as 7 − 4. The exponent is −4, so 7 − (−4) = 11.
You multiplied the masses instead of dividing. Number of grains = total mass ÷ mass of one grain.
You did not lower the exponent when changing 0.328 to 3.28. 0.328 × 10<sup>11</sup> = 3.28 × 10<sup>10</sup>.

items.prompt: A concrete mix uses cement, sand, and gravel in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 by volume. A worker needs 18 cubic feet of mix in all. How many cubic feet of sand are needed?
items.explain:
Add the parts of the ratio: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 parts.

Each part is 18 ÷ 6 = 3 cubic feet.

Sand is 2 parts: 2 × 3 = 6 cubic feet.

Check: cement 3 + sand 6 + gravel 9 = 18 cubic feet. A common error is to use 18 × 2/3 = 12, treating sand as 2 out of 3 parts instead of 2 out of 6.

mistakes.why: You treated sand as 2 of 3 parts. The ratio 1 : 2 : 3 has 6 parts in all, so sand is 2/6 of 18 = 6.
9 cubic feet is the gravel (3 parts). Sand is 2 parts: 2 × 3 = 6.
3 cubic feet is one part (the cement). Sand is 2 parts: 2 × 3 = 6.

items.prompt: Marisol borrows $4,500 to buy a used car. The loan charges 6% simple interest per year, and she repays it in 3 years. What is the total amount she repays, including interest?
items.explain:
Use I = Prt: I = 4,500 × 0.06 × 3 = $810.

Total repaid = principal + interest = 4,500 + 810 = $5,310.

$810 is only the interest. $4,770 includes just one year of interest (4,500 × 0.06 = 270). $5,359.57 uses compound interest (4,500 × 1.063), but this loan uses simple interest.
why: $810 is only the interest. Add the $4,500 principal: $5,310.
$4,770 includes just one year of interest ($270). The loan lasts 3 years: 4,500 × 0.06 × 3 = $810.
This uses compound interest (4,500 × 1.06<sup>3</sup>). Simple interest uses I = Prt on the original principal only.

items.prompt: Arrange the five numbers below in order. Place the smallest value in the first box and the largest value in the last box.
items.explain:
Write each number as a decimal:

(1/2)2 = 1/4 = 0.25

2−3 = 1/23 = 1/8 = 0.125

3/20 = 0.15

√0.09 = 0.3, because 0.3 × 0.3 = 0.09

Order from least to greatest: 0.1, 2−3, 3/20, (1/2)2, √0.09.

A negative exponent does not make a number negative: 2−3 is a small positive number. Also, √0.09 is 0.3, not 0.03.
items.why: The most common errors are putting 2<sup>−3</sup> first because the exponent is negative, or treating √0.09 as 0.03. 2<sup>−3</sup> = 1/8 = 0.125 (positive) and √0.09 = 0.3, so the order is 0.1, 2<sup>−3</sup>, 3/20, (1/2)<sup>2</sup>, √0.09.

items.prompt: A tree service charges $85 for each tree it removes and $40 for each stump it grinds. Which expression gives the total charge, in dollars, for removing t trees and grinding s stumps?
items.explain:
Each tree costs $85, so t trees cost 85t. Each stump costs $40, so s stumps cost 40s.

Total = 85t + 40s.

Check: 3 trees and 2 stumps cost 85(3) + 40(2) = 255 + 80 = $335.

85s + 40t switches the prices. 125(t + s) charges $125 for every tree and every stump, which overcharges: for 3 trees and 2 stumps it gives 125(5) = $625 instead of $335.
why: This switches the prices: trees cost $85, so 85 goes with t.
This charges $125 for every tree and every stump. Each kind has its own price: 85t for trees plus 40s for stumps.
This multiplies the counts together. The charges are added: 85t + 40s.

items.prompt: A fencing company charges $28 per foot of fence plus $350 for each gate. A customer paid a total of $5,250 for a fence with 2 gates. How many feet of fence were installed?
items.explain:
Let f be the number of feet of fence.

28f + 350(2) = 5,250

28f + 700 = 5,250

28f = 4,550

f = 4,550 ÷ 28 = 162.5 feet

Check: 28(162.5) + 700 = 4,550 + 700 = $5,250.

Forgetting that there are 2 gates gives 28f + 350 = 5,250 and f = 175, which is too long.

mistakes.why: You counted only one gate. There are 2 gates: 5,250 − 700 = 4,550, and 4,550 ÷ 28 = 162.5 feet.
You left out the gates. Subtract 2 × $350 = $700 first: 4,550 ÷ 28 = 162.5.

items.prompt: A garden center sold 40 plants to a landscaper. Shrubs cost $18 each and perennials cost $7 each. The landscaper paid $445 in all. How many perennials did the landscaper buy?
items.explain:
Let s = number of shrubs and p = number of perennials.

s + p = 40

18s + 7p = 445

Substitute p = 40 − s: 18s + 7(40 − s) = 445, so 18s + 280 − 7s = 445.

11s = 165, so s = 15 shrubs and p = 40 − 15 = 25 perennials.

Check: 18(15) + 7(25) = 270 + 175 = $445.

15 is the number of shrubs, not perennials. 20 assumes the plants were split evenly, which gives 18(20) + 7(20) = $500, not $445.
why: 15 is the number of shrubs. The question asks for perennials: 40 − 15 = 25.
20 assumes an even split, which costs 18(20) + 7(20) = $500, not $445. Solve the system 18s + 7(40 − s) = 445.
30 perennials leaves 10 shrubs: 18(10) + 7(30) = $390, not $445. Solve the system to find s = 15 and p = 25.

items.prompt:
Which ordered pair (x, y) satisfies both of these equations?

5x − 3y = 1
2x + y = 7
items.explain:
Multiply the second equation by 3 so the y-terms cancel: 6x + 3y = 21.

Add it to the first equation: (5x − 3y) + (6x + 3y) = 1 + 21, so 11x = 22 and x = 2.

Substitute into 2x + y = 7: 2(2) + y = 7, so y = 3.

The solution is (2, 3).

Check in the first equation: 5(2) − 3(3) = 10 − 9 = 1.

(3, 2) switches x and y: it fails the first equation because 5(3) − 3(2) = 9, not 1. (1, 5) satisfies only the second equation.
why: You switched x and y. (3, 2) fails the first equation: 5(3) − 3(2) = 9, not 1.
(1, 5) satisfies only the second equation: 5(1) − 3(5) = −10, not 1. A solution must work in both.
You made a sign error on y. From 2(2) + y = 7, y = +3; check: 5(2) − 3(3) = 1.

items.prompt: A line passes through point A(−2, 5), shown on the coordinate plane, and has a slope of −1/2. Click the point where this line crosses the x-axis.
items.explain:
Write the equation of the line with point-slope form: y − 5 = −1/2(x + 2).

Simplify: y = −(1/2)x − 1 + 5 = −(1/2)x + 4.

The x-intercept is where y = 0: 0 = −(1/2)x + 4, so (1/2)x = 4 and x = 8.

The point is (8, 0).

Check with the slope: from A(−2, 5), going down 5 units means going right 10 units (slope −1/2), which lands at (8, 0).

The point (0, 4) is the y-intercept, not the x-intercept.
items.why: The most common wrong click is (0, 4), the y-intercept. The x-intercept is where y = 0: from A(−2, 5), go down 5 and right 10 (slope −1/2) to reach (8, 0).

items.prompt: The graph of y = x2 − 6x + 5 is a parabola. On the coordinate plane, click the point that is the vertex of the parabola.
items.explain:
For y = ax2 + bx + c, the vertex has x = −b/(2a).

Here a = 1 and b = −6, so x = −(−6)/(2 × 1) = 6/2 = 3.

Find y: y = 32 − 6(3) + 5 = 9 − 18 + 5 = −4.

The vertex is (3, −4).

Check with the x-intercepts: x2 − 6x + 5 = (x − 1)(x − 5), so the parabola crosses the x-axis at 1 and 5. The vertex is halfway between them, at x = 3.

The point (0, 5) is the y-intercept, not the vertex.
items.why: The most common wrong clicks are (0, 5), the y-intercept, and (−3, −4), from forgetting the negative in x = −b/(2a). With b = −6, x = 6/2 = 3 and y = 9 − 18 + 5 = −4, so click (3, −4).

items.prompt:
An equipment rental company charges a fixed delivery fee plus an hourly rate to rent a mini excavator. The table shows the total cost for several rental times.

Hours259
Total cost ($)230440720

The hourly rate is {{0}} dollars per hour.

The delivery fee is {{1}} dollars.

The total cost to rent the excavator for 12 hours is {{2}} dollars.

why: 80 is 720 ÷ 9, which counts the fixed fee as hourly charges. Use the change in cost over the change in hours: 210 ÷ 3 = 70.
You divided the $210 change by 2 instead of by the 3-hour change (5 − 2). Rate = 210 ÷ 3 = 70.
115 is 230 ÷ 2, which counts the delivery fee as part of the hourly rate. Use the change between two rows.
$50 does not fit: 70(2) + 50 = $190, not $230. Subtract 2 hours of charges from the 2-hour cost: 230 − 140 = 90.
$110 does not fit: 70(2) + 110 = $250, not $230. The fee is 230 − 70(2) = 90.
$230 is the total for 2 hours, which includes $140 of hourly charges. The fee alone is 230 − 140 = 90.
$840 is only the hourly charges, 70 × 12. Add the $90 delivery fee.
You added $280 to the 9-hour cost, but 9 to 12 hours is only 3 more hours, or $210: 720 + 210 = $930.
You used $115 as the hourly rate (115 × 12). The rate is $70, so 70(12) + 90 = $930.

items.explain:
Hourly rate (slope): (440 − 230) ÷ (5 − 2) = 210 ÷ 3 = 70. Check with the next pair: (720 − 440) ÷ (9 − 5) = 280 ÷ 4 = 70.

Delivery fee (y-intercept): 2 hours cost 70 × 2 = $140 in hourly charges, so the fee is 230 − 140 = $90.

The cost is C = 70h + 90. For 12 hours: 70(12) + 90 = 840 + 90 = $930.

115 comes from dividing 230 by 2, which counts the delivery fee as part of the hourly rate. 840 leaves out the delivery fee.

items.prompt:
A trailer can safely carry at most 2,800 pounds. A landscaper has already loaded a 650-pound mower. Each pallet of pavers weighs 180 pounds. Let p be the number of pallets loaded.

The inequality that represents this situation is 650 + 180p {{0}} 2,800.

The greatest number of pallets that can be loaded is {{1}}.

why: < leaves out exactly 2,800 pounds, which "at most" allows. Use ≤.
> means more than 2,800 pounds, the opposite of a safe load. "At most" means ≤.
≥ means at least 2,800 pounds. A weight limit is a maximum: ≤.
You rounded 11.94 up. Twelve pallets make 650 + 2,160 = 2,810 pounds, over the limit, so round down.
You ignored the mower: 2,800 ÷ 180 ≈ 15.6. Subtract the 650 pounds first: 2,150 ÷ 180.
You ignored the mower and rounded 15.6 up. Subtract 650 first, then round down: 11.

items.explain:
"At most 2,800 pounds" means the total weight can equal 2,800 or be less, so the symbol is ≤.

Solve: 180p ≤ 2,800 − 650 = 2,150, so p ≤ 2,150 ÷ 180 ≈ 11.94.

The number of pallets must be a whole number, so the greatest is 11.

Check: 650 + 180(11) = 2,630 pounds, which is allowed. 12 pallets give 650 + 2,160 = 2,810 pounds, which is too much. 15 comes from ignoring the mower: 2,800 ÷ 180 ≈ 15.6.

items.prompt:
A worker on a scaffold tosses a small bag of sand upward. Its height, in feet, after t seconds is given by h(t) = −16t2 + 64t + 80.

The bag reaches its maximum height at t = {{0}} seconds.

The maximum height of the bag is {{1}} feet.

The bag hits the ground at t = {{2}} seconds.

why: At t = 1 the height is 128 feet, but at t = 2 it is 144, so the top comes later. Use t = −b/(2a) = −64/(−32) = 2.
You divided 64 by 16 and dropped the 2 in 2a. t = −b/(2a) = −64/(2 × −16) = 2.
5 seconds is when the bag hits the ground, not when it is highest.
80 feet is the starting height, h(0). The maximum is at t = 2: h(2) = 144.
128 feet is h(1). The bag is still rising then; the maximum is h(2) = 144.
160 does not come from the function. Substitute t = 2: −16(4) + 64(2) + 80 = −64 + 128 + 80 = 144.
At t = 4 the bag is back at its starting height, 80 feet, not on the ground. Solve h(t) = 0: t = 5.
h(6) = −576 + 384 + 80 = −112, below the ground. Solve (t − 5)(t + 1) = 0 to get t = 5.
You doubled 5. Setting h(t) = 0 and factoring gives (t − 5)(t + 1) = 0, so t = 5.

items.explain:
Time of maximum height (the vertex): t = −b/(2a) = −64/(2 × −16) = −64/−32 = 2 seconds.

Maximum height: h(2) = −16(4) + 64(2) + 80 = −64 + 128 + 80 = 144 feet.

The bag hits the ground when h(t) = 0:

−16t2 + 64t + 80 = 0. Divide by −16: t2 − 4t − 5 = 0.

Factor: (t − 5)(t + 1) = 0, so t = 5 or t = −1. Time cannot be negative, so the bag lands at t = 5 seconds.

80 feet is the starting height, h(0), not the maximum.

items.prompt: What are the solutions of 2x2 − 4x − 3 = 0?
items.explain:
Use the quadratic formula from the formula sheet with a = 2, b = −4, c = −3:

x = (−b ± √(b2 − 4ac)) / (2a)

b2 − 4ac = (−4)2 − 4(2)(−3) = 16 + 24 = 40

x = (4 ± √40)/4. Since √40 = 2√10, x = (4 ± 2√10)/4 = (2 ± √10)/2.

(−2 ± √10)/2 uses b instead of −b. (2 ± √2)/2 equals (4 ± √8)/4, which comes from an error in b2 − 4ac (getting 8 instead of 40; with c = −3, the product −4ac is +24, so it must be added to 16). 2 ± √10 divides only part of the numerator by 2.
why: You used b instead of −b in the formula. With b = −4, −b = 4, which leads to (2 ± √10)/2.
You got 8 instead of 40 for b<sup>2</sup> − 4ac. With c = −3, −4ac = +24, so 16 + 24 = 40.
You divided only part of the numerator by 2. In (4 ± 2√10)/4, both terms are divided by 4: (2 ± √10)/2.

items.prompt: Which shows 3x2 − 48 factored completely?
items.explain:
Factor out the greatest common factor, 3: 3x2 − 48 = 3(x2 − 16).

x2 − 16 is a difference of squares: x2 − 42 = (x − 4)(x + 4).

Factored completely: 3(x − 4)(x + 4).

(3x − 12)(x + 4) equals the expression, but it is not factored completely, because 3x − 12 still has a common factor of 3. 3(x − 4)2 = 3x2 − 24x + 48, which has a middle term.
why: 3(x − 4)<sup>2</sup> = 3x<sup>2</sup> − 24x + 48, which has a middle term and the wrong sign on 48. A difference of squares factors as (x − 4)(x + 4).
This multiplies out correctly but is not factored completely: 3x − 12 still has a common factor of 3.
Multiplying back gives 3x<sup>2</sup> − 192, not 3x<sup>2</sup> − 48. After factoring out 3, the inside is x<sup>2</sup> − 16, and √16 = 4.

items.prompt: A rectangular vegetable garden has an area of 96 square feet. Its length is 4 feet more than its width. What is the width of the garden?
items.explain:
Let w be the width. Then the length is w + 4.

w(w + 4) = 96

w2 + 4w − 96 = 0

Factor: find two numbers that multiply to −96 and add to 4: 12 and −8. So (w + 12)(w − 8) = 0.

w = −12 or w = 8. A width cannot be negative, so the width is 8 feet (and the length is 12 feet).

Check: 8 × 12 = 96. 12 feet is the length, not the width. 24 comes from dividing 96 by 4.
why: 12 feet is the length (w + 4), not the width.
You divided 96 by 4. The 4 is how much longer the length is; solve w(w + 4) = 96.
You estimated √96 ≈ 10, as if the garden were a square. 10 × 14 = 140, not 96; solve w(w + 4) = 96 to get w = 8.

items.prompt: Which expressions are equivalent to 4(2x − 3) − 2(x − 5)? Select two answers.
items.explain:
Distribute: 4(2x − 3) = 8x − 12 and −2(x − 5) = −2x + 10.

Combine like terms: 8x − 2x = 6x and −12 + 10 = −2. The expression equals 6x − 2.

Factor out 2: 6x − 2 = 2(3x − 1).

6x − 22 comes from a sign error: writing −2(x − 5) as −2x − 10 instead of −2x + 10. 10x − 22 makes the same sign error and also adds 2x instead of subtracting it. 2(3x + 1) = 6x + 2, which has the wrong sign on the constant.
why: You wrote −2(x − 5) as −2x − 10. A negative times a negative is positive: −2 × −5 = +10.
You made the same sign error on −10 and also added 2x instead of subtracting it: 8x − 2x = 6x.
2(3x + 1) = 6x + 2, which has the wrong sign on the constant. −12 + 10 = −2.

items.prompt: The function g is defined as g(x) = 3x − 7. Which expression is equal to g(a + 2)?
items.explain:
Replace x with (a + 2):

g(a + 2) = 3(a + 2) − 7 = 3a + 6 − 7 = 3a − 1

Check with a = 1: g(3) = 3(3) − 7 = 2, and 3(1) − 1 = 2.

3a − 5 comes from multiplying only the a by 3 (3a + 2 − 7). a − 5 adds 2 to a and subtracts 7 without multiplying by 3.
why: You multiplied only the a by 3 (3a + 2 − 7). The 3 multiplies the whole input: 3(a + 2) = 3a + 6.
You forgot to multiply by 3 at all. g multiplies its input by 3 first.
You made a sign error, writing 3(a + 2) as 3a − 6. It is 3a + 6, so 3a + 6 − 7 = 3a − 1.

items.prompt: Which set of ordered pairs does not represent a function?
items.explain:
A relation is a function when each input (x-value) has exactly one output (y-value).

In {(3, 1), (3, 4), (5, 2), (6, 0)}, the input 3 has two different outputs, 1 and 4. So it is not a function.

The other sets are functions. Repeated outputs are allowed: in {(−2, 3), (0, 3), (2, 3), (4, 3)} every input still has only one output, and in {(0, 0), (1, 1), (−1, 1), (2, 4)} the inputs 1 and −1 share an output, which is fine.
why: This is a function: each input has only one output. Repeating the same output (3) is allowed.
This is a function: every input 1, 2, 3, 4 appears once with one output.
This is a function: 1 and −1 share the output 1, but no input has two outputs.

items.prompt: Which equation describes the line that passes through the point (3, 1) and is parallel to the line 2x − 3y = 12?
items.explain:
Find the slope of 2x − 3y = 12 by solving for y: −3y = −2x + 12, so y = (2/3)x − 4. The slope is 2/3.

Parallel lines have the same slope, so the new line is y = (2/3)x + b.

Use the point (3, 1): 1 = (2/3)(3) + b = 2 + b, so b = −1.

The equation is y = (2/3)x − 1.

y = −(3/2)x + 11/2 passes through (3, 1) but is perpendicular, not parallel. y = −(2/3)x + 3 has the wrong sign on the slope. y = (2/3)x − 4 is the original line, which does not pass through (3, 1).
why: This line is perpendicular to 2x − 3y = 12 (slope −3/2). Parallel lines have the same slope, 2/3.
This has the wrong sign on the slope. Solving 2x − 3y = 12 for y gives y = (2/3)x − 4, so the slope is +2/3.
This is the original line; it does not pass through (3, 1). Keep the slope 2/3 and find b from the point: b = −1.

items.prompt: Simplify the rational expression (x2 − 4x − 12)/(x2 − 36). Assume no denominator equals zero.
items.explain:
Factor the numerator: x2 − 4x − 12 = (x − 6)(x + 2), because (−6)(2) = −12 and −6 + 2 = −4.

Factor the denominator (difference of squares): x2 − 36 = (x − 6)(x + 6).

Cancel the common factor (x − 6): (x + 2)/(x + 6).

Check with x = 0: the original gives −12/−36 = 1/3, and (0 + 2)/(0 + 6) = 2/6 = 1/3.

(x + 3)/9 comes from canceling the x2 terms, which is not allowed because x2 is a term, not a factor. (x + 2)/(x − 6) cancels the wrong factor.
why: You canceled the wrong factor. Both the numerator and denominator contain (x − 6), so that is the factor that cancels, leaving (x + 2)/(x + 6).
You factored the numerator with the wrong signs, (x + 6)(x − 2), which gives +4x. The correct factors are (x − 6)(x + 2).
You canceled the x<sup>2</sup> terms. Only common factors cancel, not terms; factor both parts first.

items.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to (x + 4)(2x2 − x + 3)?
items.explain:
Multiply each term of (x + 4) by each term of the trinomial:

x(2x2 − x + 3) = 2x3 − x2 + 3x

4(2x2 − x + 3) = 8x2 − 4x + 12

Combine like terms: 2x3 + (−x2 + 8x2) + (3x − 4x) + 12 = 2x3 + 7x2 − x + 12.

2x3 − x2 + 3x + 12 multiplies by x but uses 4 only on the constant. 2x3 + 7x2 + 7x + 12 adds 3x and 4x instead of 3x and −4x.
why: You multiplied by x but used 4 only on the constant. The 4 multiplies every term: 8x<sup>2</sup> − 4x + 12.
You wrote x × (−x) as +x<sup>2</sup>. It is −x<sup>2</sup>, so −x<sup>2</sup> + 8x<sup>2</sup> = 7x<sup>2</sup>.
You added 3x and 4x. The term from 4(−x) is −4x, so 3x − 4x = −x.

items.prompt: The volume of a cone is V = (1/3)πr2h. Which equation correctly gives the height h in terms of V and r?
items.explain:
Multiply both sides by 3: 3V = πr2h.

Divide both sides by πr2: h = 3V/(πr2).

Check with r = 3 and h = 4: V = (1/3)π(9)(4) = 12π. Then 3(12π)/(π × 9) = 36π/9π = 4.

h = V/(3πr2) divides by 3 instead of multiplying, undoing the 1/3 the wrong way. h = 3V − πr2 subtracts when the formula multiplies.
why: You divided by 3 instead of multiplying. To undo multiplying by 1/3, multiply both sides by 3.
You multiplied by πr<sup>2</sup> instead of dividing. Since πr<sup>2</sup> multiplies h, divide both sides by it.
You subtracted πr<sup>2</sup>, but in the formula πr<sup>2</sup> multiplies h. Undo multiplication with division.

items.prompt:
A line passes through the points (−3, 7) and (5, −5). What is the slope of the line?

Write your answer as a fraction or a decimal.
items.explain:
Use the slope formula from the formula sheet: m = (y2 − y1)/(x2 − x1).

m = (−5 − 7)/(5 − (−3)) = −12/8 = −3/2 (or −1.5).

The line falls from left to right, so a negative slope makes sense. Writing −8/12 = −2/3 puts the run over the rise, which is upside down.

mistakes.why: You put the change in x over the change in y. Slope is rise over run: −12/8 = −3/2.
You dropped the negative sign. The y-value falls from 7 to −5 as x increases, so the slope is negative: −3/2.

items.prompt:
Two companies rent out a stump grinder. Company A charges according to the equation C = 45h + 60, where C is the total cost in dollars for h hours. Company B's charges are shown in the table.

Hours (h)135
Cost at Company B ($)95205315

Both companies charge at a constant hourly rate plus a fixed fee. For which rental times is Company A less expensive than Company B?
items.explain:
Find Company B's equation. Rate: (205 − 95) ÷ (3 − 1) = 110 ÷ 2 = $55 per hour. Fee: 95 − 55 = $40. So B: C = 55h + 40.

Company A is less expensive when 45h + 60 < 55h + 40.

Subtract 45h: 60 < 10h + 40. Subtract 40: 20 < 10h. Divide by 10: h > 2.

Company A is cheaper for rentals longer than 2 hours.

Check: at 2 hours both cost $150. At 4 hours, A costs 45(4) + 60 = $240 and B costs 55(4) + 40 = $260.

Choosing "shorter than 2 hours" reverses the inequality. Company A has the higher fee but the lower hourly rate, so it becomes cheaper only for longer rentals; it is not cheaper for all rental times (at 1 hour, A costs $105 and B costs $95).
why: This reverses the inequality. 45h + 60 < 55h + 40 gives h > 2; at 1 hour, A costs $105 and B costs $95.
At 1 hour A costs $105 and B only $95, so A is not cheaper for every rental time.
The lines cross at 2 hours. After that, A's lower hourly rate makes it cheaper: at 4 hours A is $240 and B is $260.

items.skill: Writing a linear equation from a graph
items.prompt: A landscaper fills a sprayer tank and then uses it at a constant rate. The graph shows the number of gallons, W, left in the tank t minutes after spraying begins. Which equation represents the relationship?
items.explain:
The starting amount (when t = 0) is 320 gallons, so the y-intercept is 320.

Rate of change: from t = 0 to t = 2, W falls from 320 to 240, a change of −80 gallons in 2 minutes. −80 ÷ 2 = −40 gallons per minute.

The equation is W = 320 − 40t.

Check: at t = 8, W = 320 − 320 = 0, which matches the graph.

W = 320 − 80t uses the change between labeled points without dividing by the 2 minutes between them. W = 40t + 320 has a positive slope, but the amount of water is going down.
why: You used the change between labeled points, −80, without dividing by the 2 minutes between them. Rate = −80 ÷ 2 = −40 per minute.
This has a positive slope, but the water is going down. The rate is −40 gallons per minute.
You used 8, the last time on the graph, as the starting amount. The starting amount is the value at t = 0: 320 gallons.

items.skill: Number of solutions of linear equations
items.prompt: Sort the six linear equations below according to whether each one has exactly one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions.
items.explain:
Simplify each side and compare.

2(x + 3) = 2x + 6 becomes 2x + 6 = 2x + 6. Both sides are identical, so there are infinitely many solutions. The same is true for 5(x − 1) = 5x − 5, which becomes 5x − 5 = 5x − 5.

3x − 4 = 3x + 1: subtracting 3x gives −4 = 1, which is false, so there is no solution. 6x + 1 = 6(x + 1) becomes 6x + 1 = 6x + 6, which gives 1 = 6, also no solution.

4x + 2 = 2x − 8: 2x = −10, so x = −5, exactly one solution. 7 − x = x + 7: −2x = 0, so x = 0, also exactly one solution. A solution of 0 is still a solution; it does not mean "no solution."
items.why: The most common error is putting 7 − x = x + 7 under No solution or Infinitely many because the answer is x = 0. Zero is a real solution, so it has exactly one solution; only a false statement (like −4 = 1) means no solution.
